## 1. Purpose

This module prepares the real *Coffea arabica* genomic data used throughout the
prediction workflow. The population contains 195 individuals derived from
crosses involving the Catuaí group and Timor Hybrid germplasm. Genotyping was
performed by Capture-Seq, producing the SNP panel used as the genomic input.

The module has four goals:

- describe the genomic and phenotypic inputs used for prediction;
- align the 195 genomic profiles with their corresponding individual BLUPs;
- apply the same marker quality-control criteria to every prediction method;
- save one common object for validation, GBLUP-ADE, ANN, and model comparison.

No genomic prediction model is fitted here. All downstream methods receive the
same individuals, phenotypic targets, and retained marker panel.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

dir.create(
  "output/real/audit/figures",
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)
```

## 2. Packages and fixed settings

Three packages support the reader-facing analysis:

- **`knitr`** formats data summaries as HTML tables;
- **`ggplot2`** constructs the marker-quality figure;
- **`ggthemes`** provides `theme_gdocs()` and matching color scales.

```{r packages, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
```

The marker-quality criteria are fixed before preprocessing:

```{r quality-control-settings}
CALL_RATE_MIN <- 0.90
MAF_MIN <- 0.05
```

## 3. Genomic and phenotypic inputs

The genomic input contains individuals in rows and SNPs in columns. The
phenotypic input contains the individual BLUPs obtained from the longitudinal
mixed-model analysis for cercosporiosis (`Cer`), leaf-miner incidence (`BM`),
and the production-related trait (`LP`).

```{r read-inputs}
geno_raw <- readRDS(
  "data/dados_reais/geno_real.rds"
)

blups <- readRDS(
  "output/real/phenotype/real_phenotype_blups.rds"
)

G_raw <- as.matrix(geno_raw)

input_summary <- data.frame(
  Input = c(
    "Capture-Seq genotype panel",
    "Individual BLUPs"
  ),
  Individuals = c(
    nrow(G_raw),
    nrow(blups)
  ),
  Variables = c(
    ncol(G_raw),
    3L
  ),
  Description = c(
    "Raw SNP markers",
    "Cer, BM, and LP"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Real-data inputs used in the genomic-prediction workflow",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

Capture-Seq produced `r format(ncol(G_raw), big.mark = ",")` SNPs for the
`r nrow(G_raw)` genotyped individuals. The phenotype module supplies one BLUP
for each of these individuals and each of the three prediction traits.

## 4. Individual identification and alignment

The genomic rows use labels of the form `PROG 1_1`, where the first number
identifies the progeny and the second identifies the plant within that progeny.
The phenotype object stores these two components separately as `Progenie` and
`Planta`.

A genomic identifier is therefore constructed directly from those fields and
used to match each BLUP with its genomic profile.

```{r individual-alignment}
blups$Genotype_ID <- paste0(
  "PROG ",
  blups$Progenie,
  "_",
  blups$Planta
)

genotype_match <- match(
  blups$Genotype_ID,
  rownames(G_raw)
)

alignment_summary <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "Phenotypic individuals",
    "Genotypic individuals",
    "Unique phenotypic genomic IDs",
    "Unique genomic row IDs",
    "Phenotypes without genotype",
    "Genotypes without phenotype",
    "One-to-one matches"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(blups),
    nrow(G_raw),
    length(unique(blups$Genotype_ID)),
    length(unique(rownames(G_raw))),
    sum(!blups$Genotype_ID %in% rownames(G_raw)),
    sum(!rownames(G_raw) %in% blups$Genotype_ID),
    sum(!is.na(genotype_match))
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

alignment_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Individual alignment between phenotype and genotype data",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(blups) == 195L,
  nrow(G_raw) == 195L,
  length(unique(blups$Genotype_ID)) == 195L,
  length(unique(rownames(G_raw))) == 195L,
  !anyNA(genotype_match),
  length(unique(genotype_match)) == 195L,
  setequal(blups$Genotype_ID, rownames(G_raw))
)

G <- G_raw[
  genotype_match,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

stopifnot(
  identical(
    rownames(G),
    blups$Genotype_ID
  )
)

individuals <- data.frame(
  Phenotype_ID = blups$Phenotype_ID,
  Genotype_ID = blups$Genotype_ID,
  ID_Planta = blups$ID_Planta,
  Progenie = blups$Progenie,
  Planta = blups$Planta,
  Populacao = blups$Populacao,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

rownames(G) <- individuals$Phenotype_ID
```

The common genomic matrix is now ordered exactly as the phenotype table. The
stable `Phenotype_ID` is used as the row name passed to all downstream modules.

## 5. Population and trait structure

The 195 individuals belong to 13 progenies, with 15 plants in each progeny.

```{r population-structure}
family <- paste0(
  "PROG ",
  individuals$Progenie
)

family_size <- sort(
  table(family)
)

family_table <- data.frame(
  Progeny = names(family_size),
  Individuals = as.integer(family_size),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

family_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Number of genotyped individuals per progeny",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )

stopifnot(
  length(family_size) == 13L,
  all(family_size == 15L)
)
```

The three BLUP traits are summarized on the same 195-individual set.

```{r trait-summary}
traits <- c(
  "Cer",
  "BM",
  "LP"
)

trait_summary <- data.frame(
  Trait = character(0),
  N = integer(0),
  Missing = integer(0),
  Mean = numeric(0),
  SD = numeric(0),
  Min = numeric(0),
  Median = numeric(0),
  Max = numeric(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (trait in traits) {
  x <- blups[[trait]]

  trait_summary <- rbind(
    trait_summary,
    data.frame(
      Trait = trait,
      N = sum(!is.na(x)),
      Missing = sum(is.na(x)),
      Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Min = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  )
}

trait_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Summary of individual BLUPs used as prediction targets",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )

stopifnot(
  all(traits %in% names(blups)),
  all(trait_summary$N == 195L),
  all(trait_summary$Missing == 0L)
)
```

## 6. Genotype coding and completeness

The SNP matrix uses the discrete coding `-1`, `0`, and `1`. For allele-frequency
calculations, these values are converted to dosages `0`, `1`, and `2` by adding
one. The original `-1/0/1` coding is retained in the matrix used by the
prediction models.

```{r genotype-coding}
observed_codes <- sort(
  unique(
    as.numeric(G)
  )
)

genotype_summary <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c(
    "Individuals",
    "Raw SNPs",
    "Observed genotype codes",
    "Missing genotype cells",
    "Duplicated individual IDs",
    "Duplicated marker IDs"
  ),
  Value = c(
    as.character(nrow(G)),
    as.character(ncol(G)),
    paste(observed_codes, collapse = ", "),
    as.character(sum(is.na(G))),
    as.character(sum(duplicated(rownames(G)))),
    as.character(sum(duplicated(colnames(G))))
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

genotype_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Structure of the Capture-Seq genotype matrix",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )

stopifnot(
  identical(
    observed_codes,
    c(-1, 0, 1)
  ),
  !anyDuplicated(rownames(G)),
  !anyDuplicated(colnames(G))
)
```

## 7. Marker quality control

Three criteria are applied to every SNP before model fitting:

1. **Call rate:** at least 90% of individuals must have a genotype call.
2. **Minor allele frequency:** MAF must be at least 0.05.
3. **Observed heterozygosity:** loci with 100% heterozygous individuals are
   removed because they provide no segregation among individuals.

The same retained marker panel is used by all genomic-prediction methods.

```{r marker-quality-control}
call_rate <- colMeans(
  !is.na(G)
)

dosage <- G + 1

allele_frequency <- colMeans(
  dosage,
  na.rm = TRUE
) / 2

maf <- pmin(
  allele_frequency,
  1 - allele_frequency
)

observed_heterozygosity <- colMeans(
  G == 0,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

marker_variance <- apply(
  G,
  2,
  var,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

pass_call_rate <- call_rate >= CALL_RATE_MIN
pass_maf <- maf >= MAF_MIN
pass_heterozygosity <- observed_heterozygosity < 1

keep_marker <- (
  pass_call_rate &
  pass_maf &
  pass_heterozygosity
)

marker_qc <- data.frame(
  Marker = colnames(G),
  Call_Rate = call_rate,
  Allele_Frequency = allele_frequency,
  MAF = maf,
  Observed_Heterozygosity = observed_heterozygosity,
  Variance = marker_variance,
  Pass_Call_Rate = pass_call_rate,
  Pass_MAF = pass_maf,
  Pass_Heterozygosity = pass_heterozygosity,
  Keep = keep_marker,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

qc_summary <- data.frame(
  Criterion = c(
    "Raw SNPs",
    "Call rate < 0.90",
    "MAF < 0.05",
    "100% observed heterozygosity",
    "Total SNPs removed",
    "SNPs retained"
  ),
  Markers = c(
    ncol(G),
    sum(!pass_call_rate),
    sum(!pass_maf),
    sum(!pass_heterozygosity),
    sum(!keep_marker),
    sum(keep_marker)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

qc_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Marker quality-control summary",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

The retained panel contains `r format(sum(keep_marker), big.mark = ",")` SNPs
from the `r format(ncol(G), big.mark = ",")` raw Capture-Seq markers.

### 7.1 Minor allele frequency

The MAF distribution summarizes allele-frequency balance across the raw marker
panel. The vertical line indicates the minimum MAF retained for prediction.

```{r maf-distribution, fig.cap="Minor allele frequency distribution across the raw Capture-Seq SNP panel. The dashed line indicates the MAF threshold used for marker retention."}
maf_plot_data <- data.frame(
  MAF = maf,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

p_maf <- ggplot(
  maf_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = MAF
  )
) +
  geom_density(
    alpha = 0.28,
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = MAF_MIN,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Minor allele frequency",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_gdocs()

print(p_maf)
```

```{r save-maf-tiff, include=FALSE}
ggsave(
  "output/real/audit/figures/marker_maf_distribution.tiff",
  plot = p_maf,
  device = "tiff",
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```

## 8. Common marker panel

The quality-control rules are applied once to create the marker matrix shared by
all downstream prediction methods.

```{r common-marker-panel}
G_qc <- G[
  ,
  keep_marker,
  drop = FALSE
]

retained_call_rate <- call_rate[
  keep_marker
]

retained_maf <- maf[
  keep_marker
]

retained_heterozygosity <- observed_heterozygosity[
  keep_marker
]

retained_variance <- marker_variance[
  keep_marker
]

marker_contract <- data.frame(
  Property = c(
    "Individuals",
    "Retained SNPs",
    "Minimum call rate",
    "Minimum MAF",
    "Maximum observed heterozygosity",
    "Minimum marker variance"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(G_qc),
    ncol(G_qc),
    min(retained_call_rate),
    min(retained_maf),
    max(retained_heterozygosity),
    min(retained_variance)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

marker_contract |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Common genomic marker panel after quality control",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(G_qc) == 195L,
  all(retained_call_rate >= CALL_RATE_MIN),
  all(retained_maf >= MAF_MIN),
  all(retained_heterozygosity < 1),
  all(retained_variance > 0),
  !anyDuplicated(colnames(G_qc))
)
```

The final genomic matrix therefore contains `r nrow(G_qc)` individuals and
`r format(ncol(G_qc), big.mark = ",")` SNPs. The `-1/0/1` genotype coding and
the SNP column order are preserved.

## 9. Shared object for genomic prediction

The common object keeps the aligned individuals, the three prediction targets,
the retained genotype matrix, progeny membership, marker-level quality
statistics, and the fixed preprocessing settings.

```{r build-common-object}
phenotype_targets <- blups[
  ,
  c(
    "Phenotype_ID",
    "Cer",
    "BM",
    "LP"
  )
]

real_common <- list(
  genotype = G_qc,
  phenotype = phenotype_targets,
  individuals = individuals,
  traits = traits,
  family = setNames(
    family,
    individuals$Phenotype_ID
  ),
  marker_qc = marker_qc,
  metadata = list(
    dataset = "real",
    species = "Coffea arabica",
    genotyping_method = "Capture-Seq",
    individuals = nrow(G_qc),
    raw_markers = ncol(G),
    retained_markers = ncol(G_qc),
    genotype_coding = c(-1, 0, 1),
    dosage_conversion = "G + 1",
    call_rate_threshold = CALL_RATE_MIN,
    maf_threshold = MAF_MIN,
    heterozygosity_rule = "observed heterozygosity < 1",
    progenies = length(unique(family))
  )
)
```

```{r save-common-outputs, include=FALSE}
saveRDS(
  real_common,
  "output/real/audit/preprocessed_real_common.rds",
  compress = "gzip"
)

write.csv(
  marker_qc,
  "output/real/audit/real_marker_qc.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  qc_summary,
  "output/real/audit/real_qc_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  trait_summary,
  "output/real/audit/real_trait_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  family_table,
  "output/real/audit/real_family_structure.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  individuals,
  "output/real/audit/real_individual_map.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## 10. Prepared input for the next modules

The real-data workflow proceeds with one common dataset:

- 195 individuals from 13 progenies;
- individual BLUPs for `Cer`, `BM`, and `LP`;
- `r format(ncol(G_qc), big.mark = ",")` SNPs after marker quality control;
- genotype coding `-1/0/1`;
- identical individuals, marker panel, and prediction targets for every
  downstream method.

The next module defines the common validation design before GBLUP-ADE and ANN
are fitted.
